subject: SLO acceptance pathway — hosted vs incumbent
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Mehta <sanjay.mehta@veridian.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-11T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: SLO acceptance pathway — hosted vs incumbent

Hi Sanjay — great conversation earlier. Quick recap and the items we need to align on to run a fair p95/p99 acceptance test between Redwood hosted and your current provider. Aiming to keep this tight so engineering can kick off next week if you confirm.

Recap from our call:
- Veridian target for user-facing inference: p95 <= 250ms, p99 <= 480ms (end-to-end across your client -> Redwood -> model -> response).
- Typical steady-state traffic: 120 QPS for the profile we discussed, bursts up to ~400 QPS for 30s during peak.
- Streaming expectations: bi-directional streaming for partial outputs, max concurrent streams per session: 1, but up to 75 concurrent streaming sessions from a single region.
- Payloads: median input tokens ~45, tail to 512 tokens for long-form notes.

What we need from you to finalize the POC test plan:
1) Confirm the exact p95/p99 numbers you currently measure (include measurement window and percentiles source).
2) Share representative trace samples (latency breakdowns including client network, gateway, provider side) and any throttling rules.
3) Confirm whether you require header-preserving routing or custom API token headers for traffic shaping/attribution.
4) Allowlist our POC egress IPs and provide a test API key or a sandbox endpoint we can hit.

Proposed next steps (if you confirm items above):
- Redwood runs a 48-hour A/B test: 24 hours routed to incumbent, 24 hours to Redwood hosted, with identical synthetic traffic and your production trace replay.
- We provide p95/p99, median, and absolute tail traces per minute, plus a token-level cost estimate for the observed traffic profile.
- Fail-open policy: if Redwood misses p99 target by >20% for two consecutive 5-minute windows, traffic automatically routes back to incumbent and we pause the test for investigation.

Attachments: I had our engineering team flag the runbook and we requested a few trace samples. If you can drop the incumbent export (CSV/XLSX) that would help us calibrate the traffic generator.

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0147

From: Sanjay Mehta <sanjay.mehta@veridian.ai>

Cc: Emma Hollis <emma.hollis@veridian.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-11T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLO acceptance pathway — hosted vs incumbent

Thanks for the clear summary, Rafael. I attached the incumbent metrics export (veridian_incumbent_metrics.xlsx) and a trimmed set of raw traces (veridian_p95_p99_trace_samples.csv). A few clarifications inline: 

- Our reported numbers: p95 ~ 210ms, p99 ~ 430ms (measured at our API gateway, 1-week rolling window). We include network time in our numbers; instrumented breakdown is in the CSV.
- Throughput: baseline is actually closer to 100 QPS during working hours, but we have scheduled batch spikes that hit 380 QPS for 20-40s.
- Streaming: we use server-sent increments; partial output latency matters to UX — we typically expect the first token within 120ms for short prompts. For long prompts the streaming window is more lenient.
- Throttles: we enforce a soft concurrency limit of 200 concurrent sessions / region with token-based backpressure.

One ask: can Redwood reproduce the same network conditions (simulated client egress latency) so the comparison is apples-to-apples? We can provide a small capture of RTT distributions.

Attached: veridian_incumbent_metrics.xlsx, veridian_p95_p99_trace_samples.csv

Sanjay Mehta
Head of Platform Engineering | Veridian Health
sanjay.mehta@veridian.ai

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Mehta <sanjay.mehta@veridian.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-12T09:11:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLO acceptance pathway — hosted vs incumbent

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the files — that helps a lot. Proposed POC test plan (technical):

1) Pre-POC checklist (action items for Veridian):
   - Provide a sandbox API key or endpoint (valid for 72h) so we don't hit prod quotas.
   - Allowlist Redwood POC egress CIDR: 34.200.120.0/22, 3.101.34.0/24 (we'll provide final list).
   - Share RTT distribution capture (we'll replay network delay on our side to match).

2) POC execution (Redwood + Veridian):
   - Day 0 (ramp): Validate headers, token attribution, sanity-check single-threaded requests.
   - Day 1: Incumbent baseline replay (24h) — we replay your traces against your current provider using our test harness so we can ensure parity in the generator.
   - Day 2: Redwood hosted run (24h) — same generator, same windows. We collect per-minute p95/p99 and full request traces for the top 5 slowest endpoints.

3) Traffic profile & measurement specifics:
   - Traffic to match median input size: 45 tokens, tail to 512 tokens.
   - Concurrency: sustained 120 QPS, burst up to 400 QPS for 30-40s.
   - Streaming: validate first-byte latency separately — target first-byte p95 <= 150ms for short prompts.

4) Acceptance criteria:
   - Primary: Redwood p99 must be <= incumbent p99 * 1.15 (15% slack) OR absolute p99 <= 480ms.
   - Secondary: First-byte streaming p95 must be <= incumbent first-byte p95 + 50ms.

If that looks good, we'll schedule the runs. Proposed slots: Aug 19–20 for baseline + Aug 21–22 for Redwood, or we can compress into back-to-back 48h window if you prefer.

We'll produce a short report with latency percentiles, request-level traces, and a cost delta for tokens generated during the POC. Ben will own the traffic generator and analysis.

Best — Rafael
